behavior: Usually forages on or near the ground, hopping and scratching through leaf litter or snow for seeds and insects. Often forms flocks outside the breeding season; its agile, low flight exposes flashing white outer tail feathers.
field_marks: Small sparrow with a rounded head and fairly long tail
Dark eye and slender pinkish-to-dark legs
Highly variable gray, blackish, or brown upperparts contrasting with a pale belly
White outer tail feathers flash conspicuously in flight
Wings are dark and compact, usually without bold wing bars
habitat: Breeds mainly in open coniferous, mixed, and deciduous woodland, especially around edges and clearings. In migration and winter it also uses open woods, brush, fields, roadsides, parks, gardens, and other semi-open habitats.
